title: Integrated Management of Tomato Early Blight
institution: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR)
limitations: Symptoms often mimic Septoria leaf spot and nutritional deficiency in early stages. Microscopic spore check or symptom progression review advised before intensive intervention.
diagnosticCharacteristics: Concentric dark rings forming 'target board' or bullseye pattern on older leaves first
Yellow chlorotic halo surrounding brown or dark brown necrotic spots
Lower canopy foliage infected first, progressing upward as canopy remains dense
Sunken dark lesions on stem or collar in severe cases

favorableWeather.rainfallFactor: Frequent light showers or heavy morning dew with warm days

safeManagementSteps: Prune affected lower leaves (bottom 12-18 inches) using sanitized shears to increase airflow.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; switch to drip or base watering to keep leaves dry.
Apply organic mulch (straw or dried grass) around the base to prevent soil-splash of fungal spores.
Rotate crops with non-solanaceous crops (e.g., maize, pulses) for at least 2 seasons.
Consult local agricultural extension officer (KVK) for bio-fungicide (Trichoderma viride 1%) formulation.
chemicalWarning: Do not apply chemical fungicide cocktails without confirmed diagnosis. Strictly adhere to pre-harvest intervals (PHI) to prevent food residues.

title: Field Diagnosis and Emergency Protocols for Late Blight in Tomato
institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) Agritech Portal & ICAR-CPRI
region: Highlands, temperate, and humid subtropical winter regions
limitations: Rapidly destructive under cool, fog/rainy conditions. Can destroy an entire field within 7-10 days if misdiagnosed as water logging or early blight.
diagnosticCharacteristics: Water-soaked pale to dark green irregular lesions turning brown-black rapidly
White or grayish downy fungal-like growth visible on the underside of leaves during high humidity/early morning
Stems show greasy, dark brown to purplish lesions that easily snap
Firm brown blotches on green or ripening fruit

favorableWeather.rainfallFactor: Prolonged fog, continuous drizzle, or cool overcast weather

safeManagementSteps: Immediately rogue (remove and safely burn/deep-bury) severely infected plants to halt spore spread.
Strictly stop overhead watering immediately; maximize inter-row air circulation.
Inspect nearby potato or tomato fields for initial foci of infection.
Apply copper oxychloride (COC) or Bordeaux mixture (1%) preventive barrier spray as recommended by nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK).
Do not compost infected plant residues.
chemicalWarning: High-risk pathogen with rapid resistance buildup. Use only university-approved protective fungicides and wear personal protective equipment (PPE).

title: Protected Cultivation and Polyhouse Tomato Leaf Mold Advisory
region: Polyhouse, greenhouse, and high-density humid outdoor regions
limitations: Principally attacks leaves; fruit infection is rare. Often confused with powdery mildew or nutrient deficiency.
diagnosticCharacteristics: Pale green or yellowish indistinct chlorotic patches on upper leaf surface
Olive-green to velvety brown velvety mold patches on corresponding lower leaf surface
Oldest leaves curl, wither, and drop prematurely without target-board rings
Thrives under high relative humidity inside tunnels or dense shade

favorableWeather.rainfallFactor: Condensation on leaf undersides, stagnant humid air

safeManagementSteps: Increase polyhouse/tunnel ventilation, open side curtains to drop humidity below 80%.
Widen spacing between rows to avoid overlapping foliage.
De-leaf lower senescent foliage carefully to improve light penetration.
Base watering only; avoid wetting the canopy.
chemicalWarning: Avoid excessive preventative spraying; microclimate control (ventilation) is the most effective and eco-friendly management method.

title: Bacterial Spot of Solanaceous Vegetables: Field Identification and Sanitation
institution: ICAR - Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi
region: Warm, wet, windy tropical and subtropical farming belts
limitations: Antibiotics are strictly restricted in commercial agriculture due to AMR risks. Differentiation from bacterial speck requires lesion size observation.
diagnosticCharacteristics: Small (2-3 mm) dark brown to black circular lesions on leaves, often water-soaked initially
Centers of lesions frequently tear or drop out, giving a shot-hole or ragged appearance
Fruit shows raised brown scabby warts with white halos on immature fruit
No concentric bullseye rings and no downy mold underside

favorableWeather.rainfallFactor: Heavy wind-driven rain, sprinkler splash that spreads bacterial cells

safeManagementSteps: Do not enter or cultivate fields while foliage is wet to avoid mechanically transmitting bacteria.
Disinfect all pruning tools in 10% bleach or 70% ethanol between plants.
Use certified disease-free treated seed and healthy nursery transplants.
Copper-based bactericide sprays mixed with mancozeb as per state package of practices.
Incorporate deep ploughing of crop residues immediately post-harvest.
chemicalWarning: Do not use unapproved human antibiotics (streptomycin misuse is restricted). Follow national guidelines on bactericide safety.

pathogen: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (Begomovirus transmitted by Whitefly Bemisia tabaci)
title: Vector Management and Integrated Protocol for TYLCV in Tomato
institution: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Bangalore & ICAR-IIHR
region: All tomato growing tracts with whitefly populations
limitations: Viral infection cannot be cured once symptoms manifest inside the plant. Fungicides have ZERO effect.
diagnosticCharacteristics: Marked stunting and erect bushy appearance of plants
Upward curling and cupping of leaflet margins with pronounced yellowing (chlorosis)
Reduction in leaf blade size, giving a puckered, deformed appearance
Severe flower abscission and drastic fruit set reduction

favorableWeather.rainfallFactor: Dry, warm periods that favor whitefly vector reproduction and migration

safeManagementSteps: Install yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre) across the field to monitor and mass-trap whiteflies.
Erect 40-mesh insect-proof nylon nets over seedling nurseries.
Rogue out and destroy infected viral plants early to reduce inoculum reservoir.
Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Neem oil (3 ml/L) for safe botanical whitefly suppression.
Grow border crops like maize, sorghum, or pearl millet (3 rows) as barrier against whitefly drift.
chemicalWarning: Never spray fungicides against viral diseases. Misuse of broad-spectrum synthetic pyrethroids causes whitefly resurgence by killing natural predators.

title: Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for Sustainable Tomato Production
institution: ICAR - National Academy of Agricultural Research Management (NAARM)
limitations: Minor mechanical damage, normal physiological leaf curl from wind, or aging cotyledons should not be mistaken for pathology.
diagnosticCharacteristics: Uniform vibrant green foliage without chlorotic spots, dark halos, or necrotic margins
Vigorous stem and leaf turgidity without wilting
Even leaf texture without downy growth, powdery deposits, or insect galling
Healthy branching and normal flowering/fruit set

favorableWeather.rainfallFactor: Evenly distributed soil moisture with well-drained soil

safeManagementSteps: Maintain consistent soil moisture through scheduled drip irrigation.
Apply balanced organic compost and micronutrients (foliar zinc and boron if indicated).
Regularly scout the field twice weekly for early signs of pests or stressors.
Ensure proper plant staking or trellising to keep foliage off the ground.
chemicalWarning: No pesticide spray required. Indiscriminate chemical applications harm beneficial pollinators and soil microbiome.
